solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: After phone call, promise something trendy in speech (8)

indicatorNotes.After: the second piece comes after the first

blocks.note: to give someone a buzz is to phone them
to give your word is to promise

annotation.surface: Someone rings a friend and pledges to sound fashionable in conversation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you BUZZ goes first even though 'promise' is written after it anyway; the order in the clue and the answer agree.
annotation.definitionFit: A buzzword is a fashionable word or phrase of the moment.

entries.clue: Dwarf’s party at capacity, we gather (7)

indicatorNotes.we gather: to gather is to hear or learn, so what we gather is what we hear spoken

blocks.note: a bash is an informal party
full = at capacity, heard rather than spelt, so it loses an L

annotation.surface: A remark that some small person's party is packed out.
annotation.walkthrough: Said aloud, BASH FULL is BASHFUL, one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White. 'We gather' looks like the guests assembling; it is a sound signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Bashful is the name of one of Snow White's seven dwarfs.

entries.clue: Zulu mostly broadcast in former African country (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet
broadcast = AIRED, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A Zulu-language programme going out on the radio in an old African state.
annotation.walkthrough: Zulu looks like the African people and fits the surface perfectly, but it is only the letter Z.
annotation.definitionFit: Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.

entries.clue: Wizard initially yearning to tamper with healer (5,6)

blocks.note: an itch is a restless craving
to doctor something is to tamper with it

annotation.surface: A wizard longing to meddle with a medical man's work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' is there for its W but also colours the scene with magic, which the answer fulfils.
annotation.definitionFit: A witch doctor is a traditional healer believed to have magic powers.

entries.clue: Fresh tear in part of the eye (6)

indicatorNotes.Fresh: made anew, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A new rip in some part of the eye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as a teardrop beside 'eye', but the fodder is 'tear in' and 'in' belongs to it, not to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

entries.clue: Wading bird with bit of hibiscus (4)

indicatorNotes.with bit of: the answer is a bit of the next word

blocks.note: the four letters after the opening H

annotation.surface: A heron-like bird standing among hibiscus flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: h(IBIS)cus: the whole answer sits inside one word, which is unusually generous.
annotation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

entries.clue: Benefit when carrying completely inflatable item (7)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the first word holds the second inside it

annotation.surface: Something useful when you are toting a blow-up toy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' reads as someone holding the balloon, but it is the benefit word that holds the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A balloon is the everyday example of a thing you fill with air, the definition by function.

entries.clue: Father beginning to notice warning sound (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: A dad starting to hear an alarm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to notice' reads as a dad slowly becoming aware; it only supplies N.
annotation.definitionFit: A siren is a device making a loud warning wail.

entries.clue: Move computer key (5)

blocks.note: a plain verb: to budge or relocate
the key held down to type capital letters

annotation.walkthrough: Two meanings side by side with no link word between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Shift means move, and it is also the keyboard key for capitals.

entries.clue: Acrobat’s glass (7)

blocks.note: an acrobat who does somersaults and flips

annotation.surface: An acrobat's drinking glass.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as possessive but stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: A tumbler is both a gymnast who tumbles and a straight-sided glass.

entries.clue: Some sumos quit, one testing way to stop bites? (8,3)

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'sumos' to the T of 'testing'

annotation.surface: Some sumo wrestlers give up, one of them trialling a way to avoid being bitten.
annotation.walkthrough: su(MOS QUIT, ONE T)esting. The question mark flags the whimsy of sumo wrestlers worrying about bites; the answer spans four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A mosquito net hangs over a bed to keep biting insects off.

entries.clue: Enemy froze at regular intervals (3)

indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: letters picked at evenly spaced points, like posts at regular intervals, means every second one

annotation.surface: An enemy freezing now and again.
annotation.walkthrough: Take the first, third and fifth letters of 'froze'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: foe is the older, more literary word for an enemy.

entries.clue: Bequeaths, effortlessly (5,4)

blocks.note: passes on to heirs, verb plus adverb
an idiom for winning with ease

annotation.surface: Someone leaves an inheritance without any trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from horse racing, where a jockey winning comfortably could drop his hands and relax the reins.
annotation.definitionFit: Hands down means both passes on to descendants and with no effort.

entries.clue: Booze, something black and sweet, lacking ice (6)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the named letters are taken out

annotation.surface: A drink, like a dark sweet treat, served without ice.
annotation.walkthrough: Liquorice is the British spelling of licorice. The surface suggests a drink served neat; the ice comes out of the sweet instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Liquor is strong alcoholic drink.

entries.clue: Characteristic fairness abandoned by leader (7)

annotation.surface: A leader betraying the principle of fairness they were known for.
annotation.walkthrough: (e)QUALITY: the leader deserting fairness sounds political, but it is only the first letter going.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: kindness, say, is a quality or characteristic of a person.

entries.clue: One of five kids with extremely coarse fruit (6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extreme letters, first and last

blocks.note: a quin is one of quintuplets

annotation.surface: A quintuplet holding some rough-skinned fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely coarse' reads as very rough, a fair description of the fruit's skin, but it gives only C and E.
annotation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit.

entries.clue: Messed up a quote — Romeo’s line about the earth? (7)

indicatorNotes.Messed up: a quote that is messed up has its words in the wrong order, and so here do its letters

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An actor fluffs a Shakespeare quotation: is Romeo's line about the world?
annotation.walkthrough: Romeo and 'line' conjure a play script; the line is the one drawn round the globe.
annotation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary line around the middle of the earth.

entries.clue: Nurse concerned with connective tissue (6)

blocks.note: on = about, as in 'a book on birds'

annotation.surface: A nurse dealing with an injured tendon or ligament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a noun in a medical scene; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A tendon is tough tissue connecting muscle to bone.

entries.clue: Flat suitable to accommodate male painters? (9)

indicatorNotes.to accommodate: the first word holds the second inside it

annotation.surface: A flat fit to house some male artists.
annotation.walkthrough: AP(ARTMEN)T. The question mark admits that ART MEN for painters is a stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional pair: flat is the British word, apartment the American one, for the same home.

entries.clue: Endlessly examine beasts of burden (5)

blocks.note: examine = evaluate, a six-letter synonym with its final letter cut

annotation.surface: An order to keep inspecting pack animals forever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like 'without stopping'; it means without the end letter, so ASSESS loses its last S.
annotation.definitionFit: Asses, or donkeys, are used to carry loads.

entries.clue: Feathered creature eats more urgently at first (3)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: A bird gobbling its food ever faster at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: Take the first letters of the three words after the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

entries.clue: Frequent flyer well below par? (5)

blocks.note: a golf score two strokes under par

annotation.surface: A regular airline traveller feeling rather poorly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frequent flyer' suggests air miles, and 'below par' suggests feeling unwell; both are really about the bird and golf.
annotation.definitionFit: An eagle is a bird, and in golf a score two under par.

entries.clue: Prison wine is mixed (7)

annotation.surface: Jailhouse wine being blended.
annotation.walkthrough: Stir is old slang for jail.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain past-tense synonym: a spoon mixes a drink by stirring it round.

entries.clue: Dark time is unusual thing (5)

indicatorNotes.unusual: an unusual form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A gloomy period being a strange affair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the hours between sunset and sunrise, when it is dark.

entries.clue: Keys broken in Scottish island (4)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone's keys snap while on holiday on a Scottish island.
annotation.walkthrough: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Skye is an island off the west coast of Scotland.

entries.clue: Water and ink ruined woolly clothes (8)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rearranged

annotation.surface: A spill of water and ink has spoiled some jumpers.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a laundry disaster, and the answer is exactly the ruined garments.
annotation.definitionFit: Knitwear is knitted clothing such as jumpers and cardigans.
